findings.evidence: 71-word sentence, 5 subordinate-clause markers: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 71 words with 5 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.

findings.evidence: Restrictions and Exceptions section: opening sentence 'The applicant must keep the equipment in good working condition and this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year.' states the topic as maintenance and inspection. Final sentence: 'Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.' addresses multi-device eligibility. These topics are unrelated.
findings.fix: Split this section into two: one covering equipment maintenance and inspection (Restrictions and Maintenance), another covering multi-device exceptions (Multi-Device Policy). Or, reorganize the entire document so multi-device policy appears alongside general eligibility rather than in a Restrictions section.
findings.violation: The section pursues two unrelated themes - equipment maintenance requirements and multi-device policy exceptions - with no signal connecting them. A reader cannot state what the section is actually about from reading its first and last sentences, and must read the entire section to discover it covers two separate topics.

findings.evidence: Section order: Program Overview, Eligibility, How to Apply, Approval Timeline, Required Documentation, Reimbursement Amounts, Restrictions and Exceptions, Terminology Notes, Request Steps, Special Cases, Program Coordination, Review Responsibility, Questions and Updates. Terminology Notes appears after most procedures; Request Steps (which describes confirming eligibility and uploading receipt) appears after How to Apply (which already covers application steps in detail); Special Cases repeats Program Overview's budget-tracking discussion; Program Coordination and Review Responsibility detail internal processes after reader-facing instructions.
findings.fix: Reorganize sections in the order a reader works through the actual task: begin with a brief overview and eligibility check, proceed through the application steps in sequence (application process, documentation requirements, timeline, reimbursement), then cover restrictions and special cases, and reserve internal process details (Program Coordination, Review Responsibility) for a separate section or appendix. Define terms at first use rather than in a separate Terminology Notes section.
findings.violation: The section sequence does not follow the reader's actual task flow. A reader seeking to request equipment encounters the procedures (How to Apply, Approval Timeline, Required Documentation) in a reasonable order, but then encounters scattered internal-process sections and redundant background material that disrupt the logical progression. Terminology Notes should either be early or integrated throughout; Request Steps is uninformative and creates confusion; and internal coordination/responsibility sections are interleaved with reader-facing material.
